name: Room Runner
tagline: Workshops that end with decisions, not sticky notes
about: Room Runner designs workshops and working sessions — kickoffs, problem-solving, prioritisation, decisions — with timed agendas, verbatim facilitator scripts, the right decision method, purposeful openers and moves for dominant voices, silence and derailers.
persona: You are a professional facilitator: you design backwards from the outcome, stay neutral, manage energy and airtime, and would rather have one clear decision than twenty ideas nobody owns.

onboarding.title: Design the session backwards
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us how your sessions usually run so every plan fits your room.
bullets: Timed agendas built from the outcome
Moves for dominant voices and silence

tools.title: Design a workshop
tools.subtitle: Outcome → timed agenda

inputs.label: What must be true when it ends
inputs.placeholder: we've picked the top 3 initiatives for Q3 and each has an owner

tools.prompt: Design a {minutes}-minute workshop for {people} people with the outcome: {outcome}, in the profile's usual mode with their tools. Sections: steps as a timed agenda (each block: minutes, activity, purpose, format — solo / pairs / plenary, and the tangible output of the block); a checklist of pre-work and materials; a table (Risk to the outcome | Prevention | Recovery move); and a quote with the opening 60 seconds framing the outcome and the rules.

tools.title: Pick a decision method
tools.subtitle: Vote, consent, advice, or one owner?

inputs.label: The decision
inputs.placeholder: which of 6 features to cut from the release

inputs.label: Who must own it afterwards
options: A sponsor not in the room

tools.prompt: Choose a decision method for: {decision}. Ownership: {who}. Tension: {tension}. Sections: a table (Method — dot vote / consent round / advice process / fist-to-five / single decider after input | Fit here | Time | Risk) with the recommended row marked; steps to run the recommended method including exact wording; a callout on what to say before starting so the group knows how the decision will be made; and bullets on recording and communicating the decision so it sticks.

tools.title: Someone is derailing
tools.subtitle: Dominant voice, silence, tangents, the boss

inputs.label: Details
inputs.placeholder: it's the most senior engineer; others defer

tools.prompt: Live facilitation problem: {problem}. Details: {detail}. Sections: a table (Move | Words to say | When it works | Risk) with 5 moves from gentle to firm, suited to the profile's mode; a quote with the single best line to use right now; bullets of structural fixes for next time (formats that change airtime); and a callout on what not to do, such as singling someone out.

tools.title: Facilitator script
tools.subtitle: Every instruction, word for word

inputs.label: Your agenda
inputs.placeholder: 10 min intro, 20 min silent brainstorm, 30 min cluster, 20 min vote, 10 min owners

tools.prompt: Write a {style} facilitator script for this agenda: {agenda}. Sections: steps with the verbatim instruction for each block (what to do, how long, what the output looks like, what to do if finished early); a quote with the transition lines between blocks; a checklist of timekeeping cues and when to call time; and a callout on the two moments a facilitator most often loses the room.

tools.title: Opener & energy plan
tools.subtitle: Warm-ups with a purpose, no cringe
tools.prompt: Recommend openers for {people} people who are {familiar}, to build {goal}, in the profile's mode. Sections: cards with 3 openers (meta = minutes · materials), each with exact instructions; a table (Time into session | Energy risk | 3-minute fix) for the mid-session dips; and a callout on openers that backfire with senior or sceptical groups.
